newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Stately HK statue restored to Victorian glory.
newsitem.headline: Stately HK statue restored to Victorian glory.

text.p: A statue of British monarch Queen Victoria has been restored four months after a Chinese artist painted the imposing bronze figure red and dented her nose, a Hong Kong newspaper reported on Saturday.

Pun Sing-lui, a 27-year-old artist from mainland China, carried out the attack on the statue in Hong Kong's Victoria Park last September, saying his action was to protest against "dull, colonial culture", the South China Morning Post said.
Pun was sentenced to 28-days in jail for vandalising the statue of the seated monarch, which is placed at the entrance of one of the British colony's biggest parks.

Pun has since won a HK$60,000 ($7,700) prize from the Philippe Charriol Foundation as "most promising artist" for sculpture, the newspaper said. The award was given purely on his portfolio, the foundation said and included a chance to study in France.
The statue's reign in the territory is likely to be short-lived, however, despite the HK$150,000 ($19,230) spent on restoring it.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule on July 1 and all colonial symbols in the territory are likely to be removed.
